rationale.note: N_v = distinct chunk validators that must receive, verify and endorse each chunk. Mainnet RPC `validators` at epoch_height 4835 (2026-10-05): 415 validators, 10 shards; sum of num_expected_endorsements_per_shard / num_expected_chunks_per_shard = 84.0-84.1 on every shard. Independent check: nearcore 2.13.4 mandates model (target_validator_mandates_per_shard = 105, epoch_configs/mainnet/85.json:7; ValidatorMandates::sample deals mandates round-robin over shards, validator_mandates/mod.rs:134-200) applied to the same stake distribution gives an expected 84.1 distinct validators per shard per height. Several mandates of one account verify once, so N_v < 105. Re-check per season: N_v moves with stake distribution and shard count.
sources: nearcore 2.13.4 chain/epoch-manager/src/lib.rs:1064-1094 (chunk validator assignments per (epoch, shard, height))

rationale.note: Reference validator profile: NEAR's published chunk-validator spec is 'x86_64 with at least 8 physical cores' (recommended and minimal). The judge measures verify pinned to the first 8 benchmark CPUs; on the v1-6 host those are 8 physical cores (CCD0, SMT siblings idle), i.e. the reference profile. Charging allocated vCPUs x wall time (not guest CPU time) keeps the only trusted clock (supervisor wall) and makes parallel verifiers cost what they reserve.

c_cpu = 7.61e-6 USD per vCPU-second = USD 160/month for 8 vCPU (AWS m5a.2xlarge, CPU part, the first cost estimate NEAR publishes for a chunk validator): 160 / (730 h x 8 x 3600 s). The same price is used for the prover (chunk producer) because both run on the same class of node. ESTIMATE: on-demand cloud list price; bare metal is cheaper, reserved instances ~40% cheaper. Only ratios to the baseline enter the score, so a uniform CPU price change does not move CPU-only comparisons; it moves the CPU:bandwidth balance.

c_bw = per-validator network cost of one proof byte = egress price x upload amplification. Upload amplification from nearcore partial-witness distribution: Reed-Solomon with WITNESS_RATIO_DATA_PARTS = 0.6 and one part per chunk validator; each validator forwards its part to the other N-2 validators, so with N = 84: data parts = floor(0.6 x 84) = 50 and each validator uploads 82/50 = 1.64 x the proof (ingress is free on clouds). Egress price ESTIMATE USD 0.05/GB (AWS >150 TB/month tier; first tier is 0.09; unmetered bare metal is lower). 0.05e-9 USD/B x 1.64 = 8.2e-11 USD/B = 82000 fUSD/B. Not modelled: the chunk producer's own 1.68 x upload (one node, ~2% of the N_v term), compression (candidates may compress; decompression is inside verify time).
sources: nearcore 2.13.4 chain/client/src/stateless_validation/partial_witness/partial_witness_actor.rs:343-398, 442-477 (part i to validator i, forwarded to all others)

rationale.note: 0: chunk validators do not retain the witness after endorsing (only the endorsement signature enters the block; nearcore keeps witnesses only under a debug option). A future model that archives proofs for light clients would set this.

rationale.note: 0 = prepare is not charged (bench-spec-v1 section 2 policy kept): prepare runs once per verified surface, i.e. once per release, while a release proves millions of chunks (43200 heights per epoch x 10 shards), so its amortized share is below measurement noise. It stays measured, capped and reported.
